_schema: Filled in by an agent from the yurigana repo's eval runs; sites/yurigana.html renders all of it.
updated: date measured (YYYY-MM-DD). commit: yurigana commit the numbers are from.
columns: one per test set. id is the key into each row's scores; lower: true when smaller is better; fmt 'about' prints 'about N'; words: how many words the set scores; note: one plain sentence.
rows: kind is 'ours' (yurigana), 'other' (a tool it's compared with) or 'ceiling' (not a rival, e.g. an LLM; never marked best). A missing score is null.
facts: the At a glance list under the scores. label, value (code: true shows it as a command), note: one or two plain sentences.

examples: real sentences from the sets where yurigana is right and others are wrong. text is the plain sentence; word is the kanji word as it appears in text (first occurrence is the one scored); gold is the right reading; readings maps a row name to what that system read (omit a system that wasn't run). why: one short sentence on what decides the reading. Set placeholder: true on made-up entries; the page marks them and the agent deletes them.

columns.name: Modern books
columns.note: The books' own furigana over post-war novels and light novels by authors yurigana never trained on. A private library, so the set isn't published.

columns.name: Modern, hard words
columns.note: The same books, only words that can be read two or more ways.

columns.name: Older books
columns.note: 300 sentences of NDL's huriganacorpus-aozora: human furigana, mostly pre-war Aozora Bunko texts. yurigana's table was trained on Aozora texts that include these authors, so it is slightly favoured here.

columns.name: Older, hard words
columns.note: The same sentences, only words that can be read two or more ways.

columns.name: Tatoeba B2
columns.note: 27,000 sentences whose answers are MeCab + IPAdic's own furigana, so MeCab + IPAdic scores high here.

columns.name: Joyo-Kanji-Yomi
columns.note: Three checked sentences for every reading of every Jōyō kanji, rare ones included. Scored with the benchmark's own toolkit.

columns.name: Wrong words per book
columns.note: Kanji words read wrong in a typical 19,000-word book, before its own furigana fixes any. Scored against Claude Opus reading held-out plain sentences, so it is rough.

rows.name: Claude Opus
rows.note: Annotating the same sentences blind, as a ceiling.

facts.label: Furigana it marks as sure
facts.note: They cover 71% of a book's kanji words; the rest are left for the reader to look up. In a typical book that is about 65 wrong out of about 13,000. Measured on the modern books.

facts.label: Speed
facts.note: One CPU core, no GPU: a 114,000-character novel in about a second, after about 2 seconds of loading. Measured on 2,996 plain sentences of 30 characters on average.

facts.label: Install
facts.note: Python 3.10 or newer. Sudachi's core dictionary takes about 210 MB of disk (pip install "yurigana[full]" for the full one, 315 MB, the same scores); about 650 MB of memory with Jiten's frequency list loaded. A small JavaScript package does the "Known" furigana in the browser.

examples.text: この隙に逃げ出すしかない。
examples.why: As a gap or a chance, 隙 is すき; ひま (free time) is an old reading usually written 暇.

examples.text: 彼は寝ぼけ眼をこすりながら起きてきた。
examples.why: 寝ぼけ眼 is one word, ねぼけまなこ; read alone, 眼 is がん or め.

examples.text: と一呼吸間を置いて、湯どのの裡から聞こえたのは、もちろんわが心がわが耳に響いたのであろう。
examples.why: 間を置く (to pause) reads 間 as ま, a context rule.
A hole opening is 開く あく; ひらく is for doors, books and flowers opening out.

examples.text: 辛いものが苦手な人は、このソースは避けた方がいい。
examples.why: Food and sauce make 辛い からい (spicy), not つらい (hard to bear).

examples.text: そんな悪いことをしていると、いつか罰が当たるよ。
examples.why: 罰が当たる (divine punishment) is ばち; ばつ is a penalty someone gives.

examples.text: カップの縁が欠けている。
examples.why: The rim of a thing is 縁 ふち; えん is a bond or fate.

examples.text: 夜空には無数の星が瞬いていた。
examples.why: Stars twinkle: 瞬く またたく. しばたたく is blinking your eyes.

examples.text: 全ての国民は、法の下に平等だ。
examples.why: Under a law or a rule, 下 is もと; した is physically below.

examples.text: 彼の打率は三割三分だ。
examples.why: After 割, 分 is a tenth of it (ぶ), not minutes.

examples.text: この期に及んで、意見を変えるのは無理だ。
examples.why: この期に及んで (at this late stage) is a set phrase that keeps the old reading ご.

examples.text: 彼は酒を飲むと、決まって怒り上戸になる。
examples.why: 怒り上戸 (an angry drunk) is おこりじょうご, from 怒る おこる.
